card.name: Volume of diluent in preparation steps
card.fires_on: Mostly the word "of" after "volume" in dilution and infusion preparation instructions, and closing brackets after units or abbreviations like (mL) or (ANC). Also seen on a few scattered word endings and commas.

modes.label: "of" after volume
modes.description: The word "of" right after "a volume" or "sufficient volume" in dilution directions.
modes.example: withdraw a volume<< of>> solution from the bag equal to the calculated

modes.label: Closing bracket after unit or abbreviation
modes.description: A closing parenthesis after a unit or lab abbreviation in a dosing table or formula.
modes.example: infusion syringe: Volume 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection (mL<<)>> = Volume Infusion (mL)

modes.label: Scattered word endings
modes.description: Partway through a word or phrase such as a name or a term, where a count or quantity phrase may follow.
modes.example: Table 1. Status Epileptic<<us>> Loading Dosages Population Dosage Infusion

card.writes: It may push toward quantity phrases such as "左右", "以上的" and "くらい" (roughly, or more than), and away from "up to" style words like "高达" and "多达".
card.plain: It fires on the small words in dilution and volume instructions, just before an amount or total is given.
